facts.text: I want a brief for a brand positioning presentation for the fashion brand Autumn Adeigbo.
Autumn Adeigbo is described as a colorful and conversational fashion brand.
Autumn Adeigbo allows women to wear their values on their garments.
Autumn Adeigbo aims to create a positive impact on the lives of each person who touches its product, from maker to end user.
Autumn Adeigbo inspires a movement toward a more expressive and colorful world.
Autumn Adeigbo supports women standing out from the crowd and supporting each other across cultures through its product.
Autumn Adeigbo is described as the first-to-mind brand for cool, ethical, and globally influenced fashion and lifestyle products.
Autumn Adeigbo’s mission is culture, color, and conscience.
Autumn Adeigbo’s culture pillar emphasizes diversity seen in its team, customers, and marketing initiatives.
Autumn Adeigbo is described as a globally sourced brand that connects women across cultures through its products.
Autumn Adeigbo’s founder is described as a self-made founder.
Autumn Adeigbo’s color pillar emphasizes vibrant prints and color as inspiration for its collection.
Autumn Adeigbo’s girl is described as the bright spot of every room she enters.
Autumn Adeigbo’s conscience pillar emphasizes prioritizing people and planet alongside profit.
Autumn Adeigbo’s made-to-order clothing is manufactured in the USA in women-owned factories.
Autumn Adeigbo is committed to ethical practices and makes a habit of giving back.
I asked for the size of the culturally-inspired fashion products market.
I asked what customers’ pain points are in the sustainable market and the culturally inspired marketing space.
I asked for potential customer solutions Autumn Adeigbo could offer based on the pain points.
I created a customer solution to the customer pain point that sustainable fashion products are often more expensive than conventional products.
I created a customer solution addressing cost and availability barriers for sustainable fashion products.
I noted that limited availability can make it hard for customers to find sustainable fashion products that meet their needs.
I noted that limited availability can also make it hard for customers to find culturally-inspired fashion products that meet their needs.
I suggested using diverse distribution channels and offering products at different price points.
I suggested being willing to invest in high quality premium products made by global artisans paid fairly that will last a long time.
I asked whether diverse distribution and a diverse range of products can go underneath one umbrella.
I asked to create a customer solution around inclusivity based on customer pain points including cost and lack of cultural authenticity.
I identified a pain point that some customers struggle to find culturally-inspired fashion products that accurately reflect their cultural heritage.
I identified a pain point that some brands may use cultural motifs and symbols in an insensitive or inauthentic way.
